---
title: "What is the most frequent category, including ties?"
---

## The question

What is the most frequent category, including ties?

## What to check and do

1. Count each distinct category. 2. Identify the largest count. 3. Report all categories tied for that count.

## Worked example: mtcars

This example uses a public dataset distributed with R. It does not make claims about observations outside that dataset.

```{r}
#| eval: false
d <- ru_data("mtcars")
answer <- ru_apply("categorical_mode", data=d, x="cyl")
stopifnot(length(answer)>=1L)
```

The returned cylinder category is the mode of the recorded cars. This is the statistical mode, not R's mode() function for storage types.

## Apply the method to another question

Replace the data frame and column names with those in your own file:

```r
ru_apply("categorical_mode", data=your_data, x="category_column")
```

A dataset can be multimodal; the code returns all tied modes rather than choosing one arbitrarily.


## Inspect conditions

Use `ru_plan("categorical_mode")` for available-versus-missing input routes. A calculation can run even when its assumptions do not justify an inference.
